continuous_numerical.name: Continuous Numerical
continuous_numerical.description: Numeric data that can take any value within a range (e.g. height, price, speed).
continuous_numerical.model_handling: Requires scaling (MinMax or Standard) for distance-based models. Highly compatible with regression algorithms.

discrete_numerical.name: Discrete Numerical
discrete_numerical.description: Numeric data that represents countable items (e.g. number of children, item counts).
discrete_numerical.model_handling: Can be treated as continuous or encoded if the range of unique values is small.

nominal.name: Nominal Categorical
nominal.description: Categorical data without any natural order (e.g. color, city, department).
nominal.model_handling: Must be encoded (One-Hot for low cardinality, Target Encoding for high cardinality) before feeding to most ML models.

ordinal.name: Ordinal Categorical
ordinal.description: Categorical data with a defined order or ranking (e.g. low/med/high, customer ratings).
ordinal.model_handling: Should be ordinally encoded to preserve the sequential distance information between categories.

binary.name: Binary
binary.description: Variables containing exactly two distinct states (e.g. pass/fail, yes/no).
binary.model_handling: Represented as 0 and 1. Highly suitable for classification targets.

boolean.name: Boolean
boolean.model_handling: Converted directly to binary numeric format (1/0).

identifier.name: Identifier
identifier.description: Unique key or record identifier (e.g. Student_ID, UUID).
identifier.model_handling: Should be removed from training data because it contains no generalizable predictive power and causes overfitting.

datetime.name: DateTime
datetime.model_handling: Requires feature engineering (extracting hour, day of week, month, elapsed time) before being used by ML models.

text.name: Text
text.description: Rich, free-form textual sentences or paragraphs.
text.model_handling: Requires Natural Language Processing techniques (TF-IDF, word embeddings, tokenization) for tabular modeling.

geographic_coordinate.name: Geographic Coordinate
geographic_coordinate.model_handling: Can be used directly to calculate distance metrics or mapped into clusters (K-Means) for geographic grouping.
